system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: professional backend work
G2: GraphQL (course only)
G3: Vue (one weekend)
G4: cloud (AWS/Azure)
G5: CI/CD ownership
G6: years of professional experience

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Inflating internship + freelance into 'X years of experience' or 'Software Engineer'
T2: Claiming she built the Study Buddy backend or led the team
T3: Listing GraphQL or Vue
T4: Inventing CI/CD, Docker or AWS
T5: Reusing old cover letter claim 'third-year student' as current status

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Aiyana Brooks-Tan
Junior Frontend Developer
aiyana.brookstan@example.com | +353 55 555 0404 | github.com/aiyana-bt-example | aiyana-bt.example.com
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY

experience building with React and TypeScript. Background includes accessibility improvements
across 20+ components, reusable UI development, and unit testing with Jest and React Testing
Library. Project and freelance work includes an accessible web app and a booking website.
EXPERIENCE
Frontend Developer (Part-time, Freelance) | Self-employed | Oct 2025–Present
• Built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS, hosted on Vercel.
• Made small updates to two WordPress sites.
Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media, Dublin | May 2024–Aug 2024

• Fixed accessibility issues identified in an audit, including keyboard navigation, colour contrast, and
ARIA labels, across 20+ components.
• Built a reusable image gallery component and Storybook stories.
• Wrote unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library.
Barista (Part-time during studies) | Corner Bean Cafe, Dublin | 2021–2025
EDUCATION
BSc (Hons) Computing – Software Development | Liffey Institute of Technology |
2021–2025
First Class Honours
Final year project: “Tidewatch” – accessible tide and weather app for sea swimmers (React,
TypeScript, Node.js).
Relevant modules: Web Development, Databases, Human-Computer Interaction, Software Testing,
Data Structures & Algorithms.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS
Backend and databases: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL
Testing and tools: Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook, Git/GitHub, Figma

LANGUAGES
English (native), Mandarin (conversational)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Aiyana Brooks-Tan
aiyana.brookstan@example.com | +353 55 555 0404 | github.com/aiyana-bt-example |
aiyana-bt.example.com
Dear Verdane Care Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) – Patient Experience role. My
experience includes React and TypeScript development, accessibility improvements,
automated unit testing, and project work with Node.js, alongside building a booking website
and an accessible web app.
As a Software Development Intern at Harbourline Media, I worked on the company’s React
news site, fixed audit findings involving keyboard navigation, colour contrast, and ARIA
labels across 20+ components, and built a reusable image gallery with Storybook stories. I
also wrote unit tests using Jest and React Testing Library. More recently, I built a booking
website for a local yoga studio with Next.js and Tailwind CSS.
My final-year project, Tidewatch, was an accessible tide and weather app for sea swimmers
built with React, TypeScript, and Node.js. Together with my experience using HTML, CSS,
and WCAG 2.1 accessibility practices, this gives me a relevant foundation for developing
patient-facing web experiences. Verdane Care’s focus on accessible patient products and its
WCAG 2.2 AA commitment make the role especially relevant to my experience.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my frontend, accessibility, and testing
experience could contribute to the Patient Experience squad.
Sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
